newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-HODGSON ENDS SPECULATION ABOUT HIS FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HODGSON ENDS SPECULATION ABOUT HIS FUTURE.

text.p: English coach Roy Hodgson ended speculation about his future on Wednesday when he extended his contract with Italian league leaders Internationale by two years.
"Roy Hodgson has officially renewed his contract until June 30, 1999," Inter said in a statement.
Earlier, club sources said the former coach of the Swiss national squad had turned down an offer to join former English premier league champions Blackburn.
"He's not mad," said one source. "You don't leave for a team way down the premier league when you're coaching the team at the top of serie A."
Hodgson joined Inter last October and had signed a contract until June 1997.
News of his extended contract came after Inter overwhelmed Boavista of Portugal 5-1 on Tuesday night in a UEFA Cup third round first leg tie that virtually ensured them a place in the quarter-finals.
Hodgson, whose job was the focus of media speculation earlier in the season, was quoted on Wednesday as saying he would stay with Inter "until 2005" if he had the chance.
